promoter-calculator-biophysical-346param.circularity_note: CHECKED 2026-10-31 and CLEARED, the half of the open flag that mattered most. The Promoter Calculator (LaFleur, Hossain & Salis 2022, Nature Communications, PMC9440211) was fit on the Salis lab's OWN library of 14,206 designed sigma70 variants built by oligopool synthesis, validated on 17,396 promoters; its 346 parameters are dG terms for RNAP/sigma70 binding and bubble formation. GSE108535 (Urtecho, Tripp, Insigne, Kim & Kosuri, Biochemistry 2019) is a DIFFERENT library from a DIFFERENT lab and does not appear as a training source. This matters because these 346 params are the max_tx channel at 0.3968 -- the best single arm here -- and a component of the 0.4254 hybrid and the 0.4404 stack; had it been circular the three strongest numbers on this criterion would have needed retraction. RESIDUAL CAVEAT: both are DESIGNED sigma70 variant panels, so this is sequence-independence, not assay-type independence. Rests on the paper's PMC record and the authors' conference abstract, not a line-by-line read of its supplementary training tables. See wiki/promoteratlas_circularity_2026-10-31.md.

promoteratlas-base-embeddings-frozen-150.circularity_lead_withdrawn: The 2026-10-31 'worse lead' in wiki/promoteratlas_circularity_2026-10-31.md is WITHDRAWN as NOT SUPPORTED. It held that the arm might be circular on the MEASURED tile/fragment rung via the Urtecho GENOME-WIDE study (321,123 sheared fragments = GSE144621), which would have made the arm inadmissible rather than merely low-merit. The weights manifest is complete and lists five prediction heads -- urtecho2018, lafleur2022, hossain2020, yu2021, kosuri2013(translation) -- and NO genome-wide/tiling Urtecho head exists; the base corpus is genome FASTA, not MPRA. The 321,123 match was a numerical coincidence with the same lab's LATER study, which this model does not use. Recorded as a lead and not a finding at the time, which is why withdrawing it costs nothing.
promoteratlas-base-embeddings-frozen-150.circularity_note: RESOLVED 2026-10-31 by reading the weights manifest and the pretraining corpus, and it resolves in TWO parts that must not be collapsed. (1) The FLAG'S OWN QUESTION IS ANSWERED YES: a head 'promoteratlas-trspred-urtecho2018.pt -- Transcription prediction based on Urtecho et al. 2018' EXISTS, and 'Urtecho et al. 2018' is the sigma70 variant library (bioRxiv 207332 posted 2018-01-28; Biochemistry online Dec 2018, 58(11):1539-1551; 10,898 designed promoters) = GSE108535. So that head IS circular on the sigma70 rung and must NEVER be used as a comparator there. (2) THE ARM DOES NOT USE THAT HEAD. It declares the BASE model's FROZEN EMBEDDINGS, and the base corpus (HuggingFace LCoppens/PromoterAtlas-data, named in the README as 'the data used to train the base model') is 3,371 genome FASTA files keyed by RefSeq assembly accession plus one packed sequence_dataset.h5 and one segmentation_data.csv -- GENOMIC SEQUENCE, with NO expression or MPRA measurement file of any kind. Pretraining is self-supervised on sequence. So the arm as declared carries no label contamination from GSE108535.
promoteratlas-base-embeddings-frozen-150.circularity_residual: SEQUENCE EXPOSURE, not label leakage, and it is a DIFFERENT and weaker concern than the flag's. The base corpus is gammaproteobacterial genome assemblies; the tile and fragment substrates are tiles/fragments OF the E. coli genome. If an E. coli assembly is in those 3,371, the frozen encoder has seen the SEQUENCES (never the labels) -- the ordinary situation for any pretrained DNA LM used as a feature extractor, but it does mean the arm may not be described as evaluating on unseen sequence. MEASURED SO FAR: the K-12 MG1655 reference GCF_000005845 is ABSENT from the corpus (checked directly), which is consistent with the repo's own demo annotating NC_000913.1 as a held-out genome. Whether some OTHER E. coli assembly is among the 3,371 is a pending accession->organism resolution; a 0-resolved lookup must REFUSE rather than report 'no E. coli', which is a broken lookup wearing the costume of a finding and did fire once here.
promoteratlas-base-embeddings-frozen-150.circularity_what_would_settle_it: SETTLED for the declared arm. What remains is not circularity but (a) the sequence-exposure residual above and (b) the standing INFERRED merit-negative, which this check does not touch: PromoterAtlas would be a THIRD sequence-learned channel beside the conv already in the stack, and on this rung every sequence-statistics arm clusters 0.2691-0.3234 while the one thermodynamic arm sits at 0.3968 -- so the next channel should carry a different PRIOR, not a different neural net. Spending the arm is now a MERIT call, no longer an admissibility one.

honest_limits: CORPUS-SELECTION EXPOSURE IS THE LEADING ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION AND IS NOT EXCLUDED. The pretraining corpus holds 66 Escherichia/Shigella assemblies (BL21(DE3), B str. REL606, UTI89, IAI39, O157:H7, four Shigella species) and its own dataset card describes it as regulatory sequences EXTRACTED FROM GenBank files -- plausibly upstream-of-gene regions. If so, 'resembles what was selected into my pretraining corpus' is itself a proxy for 'is a real promoter', which correlates with measured expression. That is NOT label leakage: pretraining is masked-nucleotide prediction with no expression term, and the encoder is frozen with the split verified identical to the incumbents'. But it is a route by which a selection signal could inflate this number, and separating it needs the corpus sequences (a 2.3 GB h5 or the 3,371 FASTAs), which were not downloaded. Until that is done, read 0.5076 as an upper bound on what this encoder contributes.

SEQUENCE EXPOSURE IS REAL AND MEASURED. The tile substrate is E. coli K-12 MG1655; that exact assembly (GCF_000005845) is absent from the corpus, but BL21(DE3) and REL606 share most of K-12's core genome. The arm may NOT be described as evaluating on unseen sequence.

A 128-dim mean-pooled embedding is the WEAKEST reasonable use of this encoder -- mean-pooling discards the -35/-10 spacing promoter biology turns on. A positional or fine-tuned variant is a NEW ARM to declare under R6, never a re-read of this one. Stated in the bar before the run so it cannot now be used as a post-hoc escape in either direction.
0.5076 against this rung's replicate-derived ceiling of 0.941 is 53.9% of achievable. Best on the rung is not close to the ceiling.
ONE rung, ONE organism, ONE substrate, 10 seeds. The arm beats the incumbents here; nothing here speaks to any other rung.
NEVER read this against the fragment rung's 0.7928 ceiling -- the census ceiling_rule forbids the cross-rung comparison.

promoteratlas-base-embeddings-frozen-150.model_identity_resolved: 2026-10-31. PromoterAtlas = Coppens et al., 'PromoterAtlas: decoding regulatory sequences across Gammaproteobacteria using a transformer model', bioRxiv 2025.07.11.664312 -> Nature Communications s41467-026-72837-3. Weights are PUBLIC and MIT-licensed at github.com/LucasCoppens/PromoterAtlas under trained_model_weights/. Base model = a 1.8M-param custom DNATransformer (conv filters + rotary attention) trained on ~9M regulatory sequences from >3,000 gammaproteobacterial species. The arm names promoteratlas-base.pt. This closes the prior blocker verbatim -- 'the arm cannot be checked while the model it names is unpinned'.

SPAN CORRECTED 2026-10-27 (measured, was overstated 2.5x): the arm's NAME carries the MAX span log10(499/3)=2.2210, but that is realised on 49 of 321,123 fragments. Median length is 244 bp = 1.9103 decades, p99 308 bp, and only 4.0% of rows reach 300 bp. OPEN DESIGN POINT for the pre-registration: fragments are VARIABLE length (359 distinct), and load_fragments' own docstring states k-mer features are the length-invariant honest default here, so a fixed-window pyramid needs a pad/crop rule DECLARED BEFORE the run.
